claims.claim: Use WCAG 2.2 AA as the accessibility target; automated checks cover only part of conformance.
Use established keyboard and focus patterns; native semantics precede custom ARIA.
Perceptual grouping supports proximity and similarity; no universal page template follows.
Target distance and size affect pointing performance; accessibility target requirements remain separately normative.
Choice reaction time depends on information uncertainty; this does not establish a universal maximum menu count.
Working memory is limited and context dependent; prefer recognition and externalized state, not a rigid four/seven-item UI rule.
Cognitive-load evidence from learning supports reducing unnecessary burden; application to product UI is an inference.
Users develop expectations for web objects; expectations vary with audience and era.
Aesthetics can affect perceived usability; they do not prove task performance or accessibility.
Goal proximity affected behavior in studied settings; show truthful progress without promising universal conversion gains.
Animation is not automatically beneficial; use it to explain change and honor user motion preferences.
Color effects depend on context; universal color psychology palettes are not justified.
Choice-overload effects are heterogeneous; fewer options are not always better.
Avoid deceptive defaults, obstruction and fabricated scarcity.
DTCG 2025.10 is a stable community report, not a W3C Recommendation.
LCP, INP and CLS are field experience metrics; lab budgets do not certify production performance.
Server rendering or prerendering helps users and crawlers; not all bots execute JavaScript.
JSON-LD is a standard linked-data serialization, not a search ranking promise.
Structured data must match visible content and be current; rich results are not guaranteed.
Canonical hints help consolidate duplicates; the search engine can select a different canonical.
Use public canonical URLs and truthful editorial modification times.
Robots instructions are not authorization or security controls.
A crawler must retrieve a page to see noindex; blocking crawling can prevent this.
Google requires no special AI schema or AI text file for AI search eligibility.
OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot and ChatGPT-User have different purposes; user-initiated fetches may not follow robots.
Claude search, training and user-fetch agents are distinct; review current documented controls.
Perplexity search crawler is not a training crawler; user-request fetch has different robots behavior.
Google-Extended controls specified AI uses, not inclusion in Google Search.
HtmlRAG found benefits retaining HTML structure in a specific retrieval pipeline; no universal ranking implication.
GEO measured visibility changes in bounded benchmarks; effects do not prove universal provider behavior or conversion gains.
llms.txt and Markdown are opt-in community conventions; broad adoption and ranking benefit are not established.
Open Graph supports sharing metadata; it is not a universal AI/search ranking mechanism.
SPA navigation needs one page-view owner; avoid duplicate automatic and manual collection.
Do not send PII in URLs, titles or event data.
Basic gating waits for consent; advanced denied consent can still send cookieless pings. This profile uses basic gating.
